subject: Order form coordination — term windows, auto-renew and exit sequencing
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jared Mills <jared.mills@blockridge.com>; Blockridge Procurement <procurement@blockridge.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form coordination — term windows, auto-renew and exit sequencing

Hi Jared / Blockridge team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Attached is the first-pass order form redline (redline_br2389_v1.docx) that aligns the MSA termination mechanics with your procurement ask. Two items I want to flag up front: 1) the standard auto-renew cadence in our platform is annual unless otherwise negotiated, and 2) termination for convenience (TFC) can be mutual or one-sided — we proposed mutual in the draft but are flexible on notice and transition obligations.

Specific asks for your legal/procurement review:
- Confirm desired notice window for non-renewal (we've drafted 60 days prior to term end).
- Confirm whether pilot seats should be grandfathered (we included an exception in §3.2).
- Agree high-level on TFC economics: we proposed a 30-day service credit if Redwood initiates commercial TFC within first 12 months to cover transition costs; otherwise mutual TFC with a 60-day notice.

If you can, please loop legal and procurement comments into the doc and ping me with preferred times for a short sync (30 min) this week.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: redline_br2389_v1.docx (Order form redline)
From: Jared Mills <jared.mills@blockridge.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Blockridge Legal <legal@blockridge.com>; Blockridge Procurement <procurement@blockridge.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form coordination — term windows, auto-renew and exit sequencing

Camila — thanks for sending. Quick clarifying questions before we do a legal pass:
- Our procurement team typically requires a 90-day notice for non-renewal for enterprise contracts. Is there flexibility to move to 90 days?
- On the pilot grandfathering: we'd like clarity that pilot customers on legacy pricing remain on the old pricing for 12 months post-exit (noting billing implications).
- For the TFC economics: would Redwood consider a sliding credit (1 month credit for first 6 months, 0.5 month for months 7–12) instead of only a 30-day flat credit?

I'm cc'ing procurement/legal to provide formal redlines next. Happy to take a quick 30-min call tomorrow if helpful.

—Jared
Jared Mills
Head of Procurement | Blockridge
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jared Mills <jared.mills@blockridge.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form coordination — term windows, auto-renew and exit sequencing

Jared — great points. Responses inline below and I've uploaded a second redline that reflects interim compromises (redline_br2389_v1.docx -> see comments):

- Notice window: We can accept 90 days for the non-renewal notice on the base term. For pilots, given shorter onboarding cycles, we were hoping to keep the pilot exception at 60 days — this is to avoid blocking short pilots that convert. If you need pilots fully covered by the 90-day requirement, let us know and we'll update.
- Grandfathering: We can expressly preserve legacy pilot pricing for up to 12 months post-offboarding; proposed language added to §4.1 (billing continuation).
- TFC sliding credit: Redwood is open to a sliding credit. Proposed compromise in the attached: 1 month credit if TFC occurs in months 0–6, 0.5 month credit months 7–12, none thereafter. If Redwood initiates TFC within 12 months, we would offer pro-rated credits; if Blockridge initiates, credits would not apply (we can mirror mutual credits if you prefer symmetry).

Cc'ing Karthik for legal wording and Naomi for billing/ops implications — Karthik, can you please review the proposed §7.3 language and advise on mutual vs one-sided credit symmetry? Naomi — can you confirm billing process for preserving legacy pilot pricing for a 12-month window?

If you're good with this path, I'll schedule a 30-min call for tomorrow and upload a legal-redlined version after Karthik's comments.

Thanks,
Camila

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jared Mills <jared.mills@blockridge.com>; Blockridge Legal <legal@blockridge.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order form coordination — term windows, auto-renew and exit sequencing

Camila / Jared — thanks, quick legal read attached (redline_legal_br2389.docx). High-level notes:
1) Mutual TFC is acceptable; we recommend symmetric economics for clarity (sliding credits apply whether Redwood or Blockridge exercises TFC) — creates cleaner exit expectations and avoids negotiation friction.
2) Notice window: 90 days on annual renewals is reasonable. For pilots, preserve 60-day exception but require written confirmation at time of pilot conversion that the pilot is subject to the 60-day pilot exit for the first 12 months only.
3) Transition assistance: add an explicit obligation for Redwood to provide reasonable handover support up to 30 days post-termination (documented in the SOW), and include a carve-out that critical security or data-transfer tasks get prioritized.
4) Auto-renew: include a one-time reminder email 120 days before term end and an easily accessible portal opt-out for contract admins; language added to §2.4.

Procurement/legal at Blockridge — if you agree to symmetric credits and the pilot conversion confirmation mechanism, we think this is signable. If you prefer asymmetric credits (credits only when Redwood initiates), please advise so we can update.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redline_legal_br2389.docx

Subject: Re: Order form coordination — term windows, auto-renew and exit sequencing

Camila / Karthik — appreciate the quick turnaround and the legal redline. Blockridge is willing to accept the symmetric sliding credit approach and the pilot grandfathering language as you proposed, with two small asks:
1) If Redwood initiates TFC within the first 12 months, the credit should be payable as an offset against the final invoice rather than a future credit — this helps our accounting close the loop quicker.
2) For the transition assistance, can we add a clause that if Redwood is unable to complete the 30-day handover due to resource constraints, we can request a short paid extension (up to 30 days) at a pre-agreed daily rate?

We reviewed the DocuSign preview and everything else looks good. I've attached a signed cover page via DocuSign (docusign_orderform_BR2389.pdf) and authorized procurement will complete the sign step shortly. Please confirm you'll update the DocuSign envelope with the final legal redline doc and we'll complete signature.

Thanks — Jared
